1.title: Deployments, Rolling Updates and Deployment Strategies
1.text: Welcome to Module five: Deployments, Rolling Updates and Deployment Strategies. It covers the exam area Application Deployment. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Understand Deployments and how to perform rolling updates. Use Kubernetes primitives to implement common deployment strategies (for example blue or green or canary). Practice with seven hands-on labs worth forty-three points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Application Deployment (twenty percent). Practice in this module: seven labs, forty-three points, about forty-four minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: How a Deployment works
1.text: How a Deployment works. The figure shows this: A rolling update step by step. Exam tip: Only a change to the Pod template creates a new revision; scaling does not.

1.title: How a Deployment works, continued
1.text: How a Deployment works. A Deployment describes the Pods you want (the Pod template) and how many. It creates a Replica Set for each version of the template. A Replica Set keeps the right number of Pods running. When you change the template (image, command, environment, labels), the Deployment makes a new Replica Set and moves the Pods over to it, a few at a time. Changing only replicas does not create a new revision.

1.title: How a Deployment works, continued
1.text: How a Deployment works. kube control create deployment api the image flag set to engine X alpine the replicas flag set to three. create. kube control set image deployment api engine X engine X stable alpine. change an image ( container image ) and start a rollout. kube control scale deployment api the replicas flag set to five. change the number of Pods (no rollout). kube control rollout status deployment api. wait for the rollout to finish. kube control rollout history deployment api. list revisions ( the revision flag set to two shows one).

1.title: How a Deployment works, continued
1.text: How a Deployment works. kube control rollout undo deployment api. go back to the previous revision ( the to revision flag set to N for another). kube control rollout restart deployment api. restart all Pods one by one with the same template. kube control rollout pause deployment api or resume. batch several changes into one rollout. The container name is in kube control get deploy api dash o json path dot spec dot template dot spec dot containers dot name. For kube control create deployment the image flag set to engine X alpine it is engine X.

1.title: Rolling update settings
1.text: Rolling update settings. The default strategy is Rolling Update. Two numbers (each a number or a percentage) control how fast it goes. max Surge. Meaning: how many Pods above replicas may exist during the update. Default: twenty-five percent (rounded up). max Unavailable. Meaning: how many Pods may be missing during the update. Default: twenty-five percent (rounded down). Exam tip: max Surge is the extra Pods allowed and max Unavailable the Pods allowed to be missing during an update.

1.title: Rolling update settings, continued
1.text: Rolling update settings. max Surge two, max Unavailable zero means: start two new Pods first, and only remove an old Pod when a new one is Ready: no capacity loss, more temporary Pods. Both cannot be zero. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Rolling update settings, continued
1.text: Rolling update settings. Other fields you meet in tasks. min Ready Seconds. Meaning: a new Pod must stay Ready this long before it counts as available. Default: zero. progress Deadline Seconds. Meaning: after this many seconds without progress the rollout is marked failed (it is not rolled back). Default: six hundred. revision History Limit. Meaning: how many old Replica Sets are kept for rollout undo. Default: ten. strategy dot type Recreate. Meaning: stop all old Pods, then start the new ones (downtime; no two versions at once). To change from Rolling Update to Recreate you must also remove the rolling Update block: strategy type Recreate, rolling Update null.

1.title: A stuck rollout
1.text: A stuck rollout. If the new Pods never become Ready (a bad image tag, a failing readiness probe), the rolling update stops: the old Pods keep serving (that is the point), the new ones show err image pull or zero slash one Ready, and rollout status waits. Read kube control describe pod and kube control rollout history, then repair or roll back with kube control rollout undo deployment name. Exam tip: A stuck rollout keeps the old Pods running: go back with kube control rollout undo.

1.title: Revisions and change cause
1.text: Revisions and change cause. Each template change makes a revision. rollout history shows change cause only if the annotation Kubernetes dot io slash change cause is set on the Deployment: kube control annotate deployment api Kubernetes dot io slash change cause upgrade to stable. (The old the record flag flag is deprecated.).

1.title: Batch changes with pause and resume
1.text: Batch changes with pause and resume. Every template change starts a new rollout. When a task needs several changes, pause first, so there is one rollout. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Use rollout pause, make the changes and then rollout resume to get one rollout.

1.title: Blue/green and canary with Services and labels
1.text: Blue or green and canary with Services and labels. The figure shows this: Blue or green and canary. Exam tip: For blue or green, change the Service selector; for a canary, the share of traffic is the canary Pods divided by all Pods.

1.title: Blue/green and canary with Services and labels, continued
1.text: Blue or green and canary with Services and labels. Kubernetes has no special "blue or green" or "canary" object. You build them from Deployments, labels and a Service, because a Service sends traffic to every Ready Pod whose labels match its selector. Blue or green. Run the old ( blue ) and the new ( green ) version side by side, each with its own Deployment and a version label. The Service selects version blue. When green is Ready, change the Service selector to green: all traffic moves at once. Switching back is another one-line change.

1.title: Blue/green and canary with Services and labels, continued
1.text: Blue or green and canary with Services and labels. Canary. Keep the stable Deployment and add a small second Deployment (the canary) whose Pods carry the same label the Service selects plus a different track label. The Service spreads requests over all Pods, so the share of canary traffic is roughly canary replicas or total replicas: one of five is about twenty percent. To go on, scale the canary up and the stable down; to abort, delete the canary.

1.title: Blue/green and canary with Services and labels, continued
1.text: Blue or green and canary with Services and labels. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Blue/green and canary with Services and labels, continued
1.text: Blue or green and canary with Services and labels. The stable and canary Deployments need different selector dot match Labels (add the track label), otherwise they would fight over each other's Pods. Extra capacity. Rolling update: small ( max Surge ). Blue or green: a full second copy. Canary: a few Pods. Switch. Rolling update: gradual. Blue or green: instant. Canary: gradual, you decide. Rollback. Rolling update: rollout undo. Blue or green: change the selector back. Canary: delete the canary. Both versions serve at once. Rolling update: yes, briefly. Blue or green: no. Canary: yes, on purpose.

1.title: Blue/green and canary with Services and labels, continued
1.text: Blue or green and canary with Services and labels. Exam tip. For "switch traffic to green", change the Service selector and verify with kube control get endpoints svc or a request from a Pod. Do not delete the blue Deployment unless the task says so. Exam tip. A manifest rejected with "selector does not match template labels" means spec dot selector dot match Labels must be a subset of spec dot template dot metadata dot labels. A Deployment's selector cannot be changed after creation.

1.title: Lab 5.1: rollback stuck update
1.text: Lab five point one: rollback stuck update. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace roll, the Deployment web (three replicas) was updated to an image tag that does not exist, and the update is stuck. Roll the Deployment back to the previous working revision and make sure all three replicas are Ready. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 5.1: rollback stuck update, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n roll rollout history deployment web. Then kube control dash n roll rollout undo deployment web. Then kube control dash n roll rollout status deployment web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 5.2: rolling update strategy
1.text: Lab five point two: rolling update strategy. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace strat, the Deployment api runs four replicas of engine X alpine. Change its rolling update settings to max Surge two and max Unavailable zero, then update the image to engine X stable alpine and wait for the rollout to finish. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 5.2: rolling update strategy, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n strat patch deployment api dash p spec strategy rolling Update max Surge two, max Unavailable zero. Then kube control dash n strat set image deployment api engine X engine X stable alpine. Then kube control dash n strat rollout status deployment api the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 5.3: pause batch changes
2.text: Lab five point three: pause batch changes. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace roll, make two changes to the Deployment web in a single rollout: update its image to engine X stable alpine and set a memory limit of one hundred twenty-eight mebibytes on its container. Use kube control rollout pause and resume so that kube control rollout history deployment web lists exactly two revisions (one and two) afterwards, and wait until all replicas are Ready. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 5.3: pause batch changes, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n roll rollout pause deployment web. Then kube control dash n roll set image deployment web engine X engine X stable alpine. Then kube control dash n roll set resources deployment web dash c engine X the limits flag set to memory one hundred twenty-eight mebibytes. Then kube control dash n roll rollout resume deployment web. Then kube control dash n roll rollout status deployment web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n roll rollout history deployment web. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 5.4: blue green switch
2.text: Lab five point four: blue green switch. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace bg, a blue version (Deployment app blue ) and a green version (Deployment app green ) of an application are both running. The Service shop currently sends all traffic to the blue version. Switch the live traffic to the green version by changing the Service, and leave both Deployments running (so that you can switch back). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 5.4: blue green switch, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n bg get svc shop dash o json path dot spec dot selector echo. Then kube control dash n bg patch service shop dash p spec selector app shop, version green. Then kube control dash n bg get endpoints shop. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 5.5: canary by replicas
2.text: Lab five point five: canary by replicas. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace canary, the Deployment shop stable (four replicas, labels app shop ) serves version version one through the Service shop. Add a canary: create a Deployment shop canary with one replica, whose Pods carry the labels app shop and track canary and run the image engine X alpine with the container command sh dash c echo version two slash usr slash share slash engine X slash html slash index dot html exec engine X dash g daemon off. Do not change the Service or the stable Deployment. About one request in five must then be answered by version two. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 5.5: canary by replicas, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control dash n canary apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control dash n canary rollout status deployment shop canary the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n canary get pods dash l app shop the show labels flag. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 5.6: recreate strategy
2.text: Lab five point six: recreate strategy. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace strat, the Deployment batchapp (three replicas of engine X alpine ) must never run two versions at once. Change its strategy to Recreate, keep only two old Replica Sets ( revision History Limit two ), then update the image to engine X stable alpine and wait for the rollout to finish. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 5.6: recreate strategy, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n strat patch deployment batchapp dash p spec strategy type Recreate, rolling Update null, revision History Limit two. Then kube control dash n strat set image deployment batchapp engine X engine X stable alpine. Then kube control dash n strat rollout status deployment batchapp the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 5.7: fix selector mismatch
2.text: Lab five point seven: fix selector mismatch. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The manifest about slash work slash deploy dot yaml defines the Deployment web (two replicas of engine X alpine, Pod label app webapp ) in the namespace roll, but kube control apply dash f rejects it. Fix the manifest without changing the Pod template label, create the Deployment, and wait until both replicas are Ready. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 5.7: fix selector mismatch, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control apply dash f about slash work slash deploy dot yaml. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then kube control apply dash f about slash work slash deploy dot yaml. Then kube control dash n roll rollout status deployment web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which command undoes the last rollout? Answer: kube control rollout undo deployment or name. Question two. What do max Surge and max Unavailable control? Answer: The extra Pods allowed and the Pods allowed to be missing during a rolling update. Question three. What happens to a rolling update whose new Pods never become Ready? Answer: It stops; the old Pods keep serving, and you repair it or roll back with rollout undo.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. How do you apply several template changes in one rollout? Answer: rollout pause, make the changes, then rollout resume. Question five. How do you implement blue or green with Kubernetes objects? Answer: Two Deployments with a version label and one Service; switch by changing the Service selector. Question six. How is the traffic share of a canary set? Answer: By the number of canary Pods compared with all Pods that match the Service selector.

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. What does strategy dot type Recreate do? Answer: It stops all old Pods before it starts the new ones. Question eight. Does kube control scale create a new revision? Answer: No; only a change to the Pod template does.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Update: set image, rollout status slash history slash undo, max Surge or max Unavailable. Stuck rollout: old Pods stay; new Pods err image pull or not Ready; fix with rollout undo. Batch: rollout pause... resume. Settings: min Ready Seconds, progress Deadline Seconds (six hundred), revision History Limit (ten). Recreate: type Recreate and rolling Update null. Blue or green: two Deployments, Service selector switch. Canary: same Service label, different track; share equals canary Pods or all Pods. Immutable: a Deployment's selector cannot change.
